claims.explanation: GW-441756 is a selective TrkA (NTRK1) inhibitor, and its antiproliferative effects require functional NGF/TrkA signaling. Sensitivity is therefore expected in lineages that express NTRK1 and depend on autocrine/paracrine neurotrophin loops, such as melanoma, neuroblastoma, and Ewing sarcoma, while resistance occurs when NTRK1 is absent or downstream MAPK/PI3K signaling is constitutively activated by mutations such as KRAS, BRAF, or PTEN loss.

features.basis: GW-441756 is a TrkA inhibitor; target expression is required for activity
NGF ligand activates TrkA and creates dependence on the pathway
Constitutive MAPK activation bypasses upstream TrkA signaling
BRAF V600 mutations drive MAPK independently of TrkA
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT, reducing dependence on TrkA survival signals
NF1 loss hyperactivates RAS/MAPK, bypassing TrkA
Mutant EGFR provides alternative RTK-driven proliferation
MEK1 mutations activate downstream MAPK independently of TrkA
NRAS mutations constitutively activate MAPK, bypassing TrkA
PIK3CA mutations activate PI3K/AKT downstream of TrkA
BDNF can activate TrkB but may also contribute to neurotrophin signaling context
TrkB expression may compensate for TrkA inhibition in some lineages
